subject: PrivRun bootstrap & module sanity check
messages:
From: markus.klein@redwood.example.com
To: irene.choi@redwood.example.com, kimberly.park@redwood.example.com, jonas.weber@redwood.example.com, ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivRun bootstrap & module sanity check

Hi all,

Following up from last week's architecture sync: Acme is preparing their private deployment (VPC/on-prem) pilot and asked us to validate the proposed IaC layout and CI gating before the first bootstrap. I attached a short PDF that sketches the module boundaries and three CI scenarios (bootstrap, incremental upgrade, emergency rollback).

Concise asks: 
- Can the infra team confirm the proposed Terraform module split (networking, enclave, bastiOnboard, storage), and call out any coupling that will break idempotency?
- Are the Helm charts set up to support incremental values-only rollouts for controlplane and sidecar components (no image changes)?
- For Ansible (post-provisioning), do we have an agreed least-privilege credential flow for certs and KMS access?
- Can security produce a minimal evidence pack for the first audit: module provenance (git SHAs), CI run artifacts, and a smoke test matrix?

I've also attached the GitLab MR diff for the initial module carve (gitlab-mr-487-diff.patch) and a CI gating proposal (ci-gating-proposal.yaml).

Timeline: Acme expects a readiness check by EOD Wednesday (2026-05-20). If that won't work, propose a blocker list + mitigations by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — I think this is a good chance to validate our private runtime bootstrap patterns and catch any idempotency blind spots before customers hit them.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: privrun-module-boundaries.pdf, gitlab-mr-487-diff.patch, ci-gating-proposal.yaml
From: irene.choi@redwood.example.com
To: markus.klein@redwood.example.com, kimberly.park@redwood.example.com, jonas.weber@redwood.example.com
Cc: ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivRun bootstrap & module sanity check

Markus — thanks for the clear outline and the artifacts. Quick pass from infra/privstack: 

- Terraform module split: overall shape looks good. A couple of observations: 
  * networking module currently exposes vars for both subnet ranges and routing policy; recommend splitting routing (BGP/SD-WAN) into a small routing module to avoid repeated plan diffs when customers flip policies.
  * enclave and bastion share a small secret mapping (bootstrap user pubkeys) — we should move that into a sealed-params module so secrets are not passed as plain vars in pipeline logs.
- Helm: charts already support values-driven rollouts for controlplane; need to add a few readinessProbe tweaks to avoid cascading restarts during values swaps. I left inline comments in the MR.
- Ansible: propose using a short-lived certificate agent that fetches signed certs from customer KMS via a JWKS exchange — avoids long-lived keys. Will outline playbook snippets by EOD tomorrow.
- CI gating: we should add an idempotency smoke job that runs terraform plan -> apply in an ephemeral env and re-plan to detect diffs. This requires ephemeral quotas; I'll coordinate with Jonas on runner capacity.

I'll prepare a minimal evidence checklist for the audit (module SHAs, CI logs with job IDs, smoke test outputs) and drop it in the Drive link by EOD.

Irene
Irene Choi
Staff SRE, Private Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus / Irene — appreciate the quick review. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Subnet ranges: we'll own the 10.10.0.0/16 block; can Redwood modules accept an overriding CIDR map (we need to map 3 availability zones inside our colocation)?
- Certificates: Acme's security team prefers cert rotation via our in-house PKI; can the JWKS agent exchange be configured to validate intermediate CAs we provide?
- Timeline: EOD Wednesday is tight for us. What if we do a readiness checkpoint on Thursday morning (2026-05-21 10:00 PT) instead? That will give our ops team time to run a preflight scan.

Also looping in Sasha from VendorNet — they will help with network cabling and collocate switch configs. Sasha, please confirm whether vendor can provide a crossover patch to support the 10.10 ranges without touching customer edge.

—Alex Ops
Acme Corp — Private Cloud Engineering
